what_its_for: Azacitidine is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML). It works by slowing or stopping the growth of abnormal blood cells in your bone marrow.
how_to_take: Azacitidine comes in two forms: an injection given under your skin (subcutaneous) or into your vein (IV) by a healthcare provider, or as a tablet you swallow by mouth (Onureg). If you are taking the tablet form, swallow it whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet. Take it at the same time each day. You may take it with or without food. Always follow your doctor's or nurse's exact instructions on how and when to take this medicine.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body size, the type of cancer you have, and how well your kidneys and liver are working. The injection form is usually given in cycles, often once a day for 7 days in a row, followed by a rest period of about 3 weeks before the next cycle begins. The tablet form is typically taken once a day on certain days of each treatment cycle. Never change your dose on your own. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you experience side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the tablet form and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is more than 12 hours late, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you miss an injection appointment, call your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible.
storage: Store azacitidine tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container and protect them from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options or medicine take-back programs. If you are receiving the injection at home, your nurse will give you specific instructions on how to store and handle it safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Do not get live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray, shingles vaccine, or MMR) while on this medicine without first checking with your doctor. Avoid alcohol or limit it, as it can increase certain side effects. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should not handle this medicine. Men and women of childbearing age should use reliable birth control during treatment and for several months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; coughing up blood; severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that you cannot control; shortness of breath or chest pain; blood in your urine or stool; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; confusion or extreme dizziness. Also call your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Azacitidine does not work overnight. It may take several treatment cycles, usually 3 to 6 months or more, before you and your doctor see the full benefit. Some people notice improvements in their blood counts and feel better sooner. It is important to keep all of your appointments and complete each treatment cycle as scheduled, even if you feel well, to give the medicine the best chance to work.
special_populations: Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor will check your kidney and liver function before and during treatment and may adjust your dose if needed. Tell your doctor about all health conditions you have. Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine is commonly used in older adults. Your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Azacitidine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant. Women should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Men should use birth control with their partners during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established. Ask your doctor if you have questions about use in children.
